Hi John / Emily —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- Use case: contextual product recommendations + short personalized snippets (<= 256 tokens).
- Key constraints: sub-150ms p95 for single-request interactive calls, high consistency on hallucination reduction for product facts, and SOC 2/compliance requirements for data retention.
- Traffic: pilot ~100 qps peak, production forecast ~1k qps (US region).

Initial model hypotheses:
- Small-to-mid parameter instruct models (e.g., 7B–13B class) with strong instruction-following for cost/latency tradeoffs for most prompts.
- Fall back to a higher-capacity 33B–40B variant for complex prompts where correctness is critical.

Quantization / throughput considerations we discussed:
- AWQ (advanced weight quant): best throughput jump for 4-bit on many models but can introduce small quality regressions on narrow factual tasks.
- GPTQ: stable quality at 4/8-bit with slightly less throughput than AWQ in some kernels.
- FP8 (where supported): excellent quality retention but requires hardware runtime support; throughput gains depend on kernel maturity.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll run a targeted eval using your representative prompt set (attached: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.json) comparing baseline FP16, GPTQ-4, AWQ-4, and GPTQ-8.
2) Provide a short trade study (latency, throughput, per-prompt quality deltas) + recommended canary rollout plan.
3) Set up a 30-min technical review with Rishi (solutions eng) to review results and finalize the production quantization profile.

I attached the prompt set you shared and our suggested evaluation matrix. I’ve also included a short slide deck that summarizes typical tradeoffs (quantization_tradeoff_slide_deck.pdf).

Would Tuesday 10am PT work for the technical review?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi John / Emily —

Thanks — noted on the accuracy and latency SLOs. Below is the short trade-study summary and what we’ll deliver in the eval so everyone has the right expectations. I’m attaching the full slide deck to share with procurement/security.

Short trade-study summary (high level):
- FP16 baseline:
  - Quality: baseline quality / reference. Expected per-prompt accuracy = 100% relative to our gold labels.
  - Latency: baseline p95 at 1k qps depends on model size (7B ~70ms, 13B ~120ms, 33B ~250ms typical on our dedicated pools).
- GPTQ-8:
  - Quality: near-lossless for many models; expected <1% delta on factual prompts.
  - Latency: modest improvement vs FP16 (10–25%), p95 improvements will vary by kernel.
- GPTQ-4:
  - Quality: small deltas (1–4%) on narrow fact-completion tasks for some models; stable for most instruction tasks.
  - Latency: significant improvement (2–3x throughput) on supported kernels.
- AWQ-4:
  - Quality: best-in-class throughput often but higher variance in accuracy for tight factual slot-fills; some models show 3–6% regressions on our benchmark.
  - Latency: highest throughput gains; p95 lower than GPTQ-4 in many observed cases.
- FP8 (hardware/runtime dependent):
  - Quality: closest to FP16 on many workloads; promising for larger models if the runtime supports it.
  - Latency: depends on kernel maturity — can match or exceed integer quant methods once mature.

Recommendations for Acme pilot (based on your SLOs):
1) Primary profile: 13B model with GPTQ-8 for the pilot — best balance of latency headroom and quality retention.
2) Canary for heavy correctness flows: run 33B FP16 or FP8 (if supported) behind an A/B routing rule for prompts where product-fact accuracy is critical.
3) Stress test AWQ-4 as an aggressive cost/throughput option on the 13B candidate, but gate it behind strict quality checks (per-prompt regression threshold 1.5% on the gold set).

Deliverables we’ll produce for your review: 
- Eval report: per-prompt accuracy deltas, precision/recall on labeled prompts, and regression heatmap.
- Latency report: p50/p95/p99 at 100 qps and 1k qps sims for each quant profile.
- Canary rollout doc: traffic routing rules, fallback policies, and metrics to monitor for rollback.

Links / references:
- Eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-evals
- Example trade study: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1trade-study-sample
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345
